17.6% of adults aged ≥65 years were edentulous
During 2011–2014, 17.6% of adults aged ≥65 years were edentulous or had lost all their natural, permanent teeth.
Adults aged ≥75 years (23.0%) were more likely to be edentulous compared with adults aged 65–74 years (13.9%).
Data were collected by dentists in the mobile examination center as part of the oral health component of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
